note: Adversarial selective prediction: choose the future window to predict; O(1/log n) squared loss upper (Lemma 2.1: <=1/k for n=2^k) with matching Omega(1/log n) lower bound (explicit 1/64 constant); adaptive window choice gains only a constant factor. Theory-only. GSE use: pre-commit the weekly gating schedule rather than re-tuning it adaptively on noise.
title: A Theory of Selective Prediction

note: Cost-based, bounded-improvement, bounded-coverage reject models share one Bayes classifier + randomized selection; proper uncertainty score preserves conditional-risk ordering; REG (loss regression) and SELE (pairwise ranking) score learners are Fisher consistent. SVM-top: REG avg rank 1.09 vs baseline 2.82 (PHISHING 0.72 vs 6.37 AuRC); SVOR ordinal: SELE rank 1.27 vs Margin 3.00 (MSD 4.26 vs 6.23). AuRC = expected bounded-coverage quality over uniform coverage.
title: Optimal strategies for reject option classifiers

note: Per-class error caps (R0,R1<=0.05) with product/additive ambiguity minimization; VC rate sqrt((d_H log n+log(1/d))/n) with matching minimax lower bound; strict deterministic feasibility can force ambiguity risk 1, randomization fixes it. BCI: product ambiguity 0.0077 (errors 0.0505/0.0450) vs Lei 0.2293; MAGIC product 0.4332 vs additive 0.5107; Phoneme product violates (R0=0.0551). GSE use: separate error caps per market type (spread/total/moneyline).
title: Classification with Abstention under Class-Conditional Error Constraints

note: SCoRE: conformal selective prediction with general (bounded continuous) risk control via risk-adjusted e-values (E[L*E]<=1); MDR and SDR risk notions; finite-sample distribution-free under exchangeability + weighted extension for covariate shift. Simulation n=1000/m=100/100 runs: tight control at levels 0.05-0.5 where Hoeffding/Rademacher baselines are valid but far less powerful. Code: github.com/Tian-Bai/SCoRE. GSE use: adopt e-value screening as the card-selection gate controlling average betting loss.
title: Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control

note: NNTD: gate on late-weighted checkpoint prediction disagreement with the final label (best k=0.05; 25-50 checkpoints). VGG16/300ep/SGD. CIFAR-10 at 2% error: coverage 91.2 vs SAT 90.3, DG 89.1, SR 85.8, MC-DO 86.1; at 90% coverage error 1.83 vs SAT 1.90, SR 2.78. SVHN at 2%: 98.5 coverage. GSE use: checkpoint/bagging-seed disagreement as a second, nearly-free gate feature.
title: Selective Classification Via Neural Network Training Dynamics

note: ASPEST: active selective prediction under domain shift = checkpoint ensembles + low-margin active acquisition + target fine-tuning + pseudo-label self-training. MNIST->SVHN with label budget 100: AUACC 79.36% -> 88.84%. Code: google-research/active_selective_prediction. GSE use: weekly regime-shift loop where the 'label budget' is retrospective analyst deep-review of the most uncertain resolved games.
title: ASPEST: Bridging the Gap Between Active Learning and Selective Prediction

note: RISAN: joint learning of prediction function f(x) and instance-specific rejection width rho(x) via double-sigmoid surrogate for 0-d-1 loss (classification-calibrated; excess 0-d-1 risk bounded by excess surrogate risk) + generalization bounds. Label-noise robustness: +6-7pp accepted accuracy at 20% noise, +10pp (Cats vs Dogs)/+5pp (CIFAR-10) at 40% noise; +5-10pp over DAC on unrejected samples. GSE use: per-pick learned abstention width with unit-denominated cost d(x).
title: RISAN: Robust Instance Specific Deep Abstention Network

note: Joint classifier/rejector for learning to defer to an instance-dependently-imperfect expert; novel cost-sensitive generalized cross-entropy surrogate, convex and Bayes-consistent. CIFAR-10/WideResNet (90.47% base) with synthetic experts; hate-speech (24,783 tweets, 5 splits): AAE-biased expert system accuracy 92.91+-0.17 vs confidence baseline 92.42+-0.40 vs oracle 93.22+-0.11. GSE use: learned router between model, market consensus, and Garrett, trained on (x,y,m) triples.
title: Consistent Estimators for Learning to Defer to an Expert

note: Founding adaptive learning-to-defer paper: defer based on BOTH model uncertainty and the downstream decision-maker's competence/bias map; joint training so the model specializes where it stays. Semi-synthetic COMPAS/Heritage Health, three DM regimes; inconsistent-DM setting flips 30% of selected subgroup predictions; biased-DM setting: system learns to defer less on the biased subgroup. Pareto fronts, medians of five runs. GSE use: competence-map audit of Garrett's own card edits (where he helps vs hurts).
title: Predict Responsibly: Improving Fairness and Accuracy by Learning to Defer

note: Stackelberg strategic classification with abstention: Theorem 3.1 (abstention cannot increase principal loss, even strategically), Theorem 3.3 (strategic agents -> higher optimal threshold, abstain more). Simulation 100k samples/threshold, x~U[-2,2], thresholds 0.01-2.0 step 0.01, gamma=0.4444, c=0.3, sigma=0.5; turning point at abstention cost c=0.5. GSE use: line-movement stress test - raise the gate as the market moves against posted picks; find the empirical turning point where posting turns negative.
title: When In Doubt, Abstain: The Impact of Abstention on Strategic Classification

note: Two distinctions for selective prediction over ranked outputs: (1) feasibility ceiling - selective accuracy <= min(1, p/c), check BEFORE tuning any gate (8 LLMs <=4.6% Recall@1 on ultra-rare diseases, so 10% coverage can't hit 50%); (2) score = shared case-level component + candidate residual (Eq.3) - the top-two MARGIN cancels the shared part and reads correctness, the top score reads presence; margin beats top score on Exomiser (10% coverage at 29.0% vs 13.3% overall) but Prop.1 proves the better gate is unidentifiable from unlabeled scores alone - must be tested empirically. GSE use: gate on model-minus-market margin, not raw confidence.
title: One Score, Two Decisions: Selective Prediction on the Rare-Disease Tail

note: JTSP: jointly train classifier + deferral policy with shared representations and a policy-gradient loss term (Alg.1 line 15); beats post-hoc thresholding, LR-on-softmax, and separately-trained policy on all four datasets x two backbones (SFRN/BERT, RoBERTa policy encoder). BEETLE/SFRN: JTSP SP 85.33/79.63 vs Policy 83.39/76.98 vs Thresh 80.74/72.68; ISTUDIO: 85.83/84.29 vs 85.03/82.95; policy-gradient ablation adds ~0.5-2.5pp. GSE use: rebuild training loop with pick head + deferral head, policy gradient on posted-pick units.
title: Joint Training for Selective Prediction
